title: Service fallback audit & customer checklist - public update
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a short, customer-facing status update + lightweight postmortem focused on the fallback behavior we observed during the 2029-11-07 service disruption. It is written for product and platform owners at customers (engineering and SRE contacts) and includes a short checklist customers can run to validate end-to-end behavior after our mitigations.

Executive summary:
- What happened (brief): Between 2029-11-07 02:12 UTC and 2029-11-07 03:25 UTC some requests to Redwood hosted API routed into a degraded fallback path. The fallback produced higher latency and intermittent truncated streaming responses for a subset of sessions tied to KV-cache invalidation races.
- Impact to customers: ~0.6% of production requests across US-EAST and EU-WEST experienced higher tail latency (p95 > 3s) and ~0.04% experienced truncated streaming chunks. No customer data was exposed. Some tenants with aggressive prefix caching saw repeated re-computations.
- Customer visible indicators (status page): partial_degradation affecting text-generation and streaming for regions US-EAST, EU-WEST. Incidents page: INF-4521.

What we found (high level root cause):
- Root cause: A race between the global KV-cache invalidation job and a new routing optimization scheduled at the same time. The routing optimization temporarily routed traffic to a fallback model variant that uses synchronous KV retrieval. When KV lookups concurrently attempted invalidation, certain requests fell back mid-stream to a slower retrieval path which caused backpressure events in the streaming pipeline (resulting in truncated chunks).
- Contributing factors: recent rollout of a routing optimization (canaryed 72 hours earlier) and a partially missed canary gating check that did not flag KV-invalidation frequency spikes.

What we did (mitigation & recovery):
- Immediate: at 02:20 UTC we disabled the routing optimization and reverted the ephemeral routing policy to the pre-rollout stable variant; streaming recovery observed within ~3 minutes for most sessions.
- Roll forward: by 03:00 UTC we rebalanced cache invalidation scheduling windows and added extra jitter; full stabilization confirmed by 03:25 UTC.
- Safety: we enforced an emergency throttle so fallback variants receive <= 5% of traffic while we validated; no customer data changes were required and no rollbacks to models were needed.

Customer-facing timeline (concise):
- 02:12 UTC - first alerts for increased p95 and truncated streaming; automatic routing fallback engaged for some sessions.
- 02:15 UTC - engineering oncall paged; initial hypothesis: routing + cache race.
- 02:20 UTC - disabled routing optimization; partial recovery seen.
- 02:40 UTC - added jitter to KV cache invalidation windows and increased observability for prefix cache hits.
- 03:25 UTC - metrics within normal bounds, status page updated to partial_degradation -> monitoring.

Short checklist for customers (what you can do now):
(we include quick checks customers can run to confirm their integrations are behaving; most are quick curl / header checks or config verifications)
1) Validate SDK/Client retries: confirm calls include x-rw-client-id and a unique request-id. Example: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'x-rw-client-id: my-service' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -v -> look for 200 + x-rw-attempt header
2) Check streaming robustness: if you use streaming, ensure your client reassembles chunks by sequence id (we recommend tolerant reassembly on missing chunk re-delivery).
3) Confirm model pinning behaviour: if you pin to a model variant, check your console route config for fallback policies (Console -> Routes -> <route> -> Fallback). If unsure, open a ticket with your route id.
4) Re-run representative prompt set: run a small prompt batch (10 requests) and watch for p95 latency spikes. If you still see issues, capture request-ids and timestamps and send to support.
5) For heavy prefix caching workloads: if you observe repeated cold-cache recomputations, add a short client-side prefix cache (TTL 30s) to smooth bursts while we finalize KV tuning.

Support attachments we can provide on request:
- Per-tenant request-ids and anonymized traces (we will redact customer content)
- Streaming chunk samples for affected sessions (anonymized)
- Telemetry graphs for your route id (p50/p95/p99, truncated_stream_count)

Longer-term remediation we plan (customer-facing summary):
- Fix: add an intra-service lock to ensure KV invalidation and routing changes do not race; schedule this as a small runtime patch (target: 2 weeks).
- Prevent recurrence: enhance canary gating to include KV invalidation frequency and streaming truncation telemetry as hard gates.
- Observability: new dashboard tile for "fallback-routed-requests" and automatic alerts when truncated-stream-count > 3 per 100k requests.

Open questions / items we are confirming (notes):
- We are still auditing whether any third-party routing dependency amplified the fallback (will update by 2029-11-12).
- We will share anonymized per-tenant impact reports on request where customers consent.

Short customer-facing FAQ (quick Q&A):
Q: Was my data exposed?
A: No. This incident impacted routing and cache behavior only; there was no unauthorized access to customer data.

Q: Do I need to rotate keys or take other security actions?
A: No security action required.

Q: Will you notify me with a per-tenant impact summary?
A: Yes — we can generate a per-tenant CSV of request counts and affected request-ids upon request. Open a support ticket referencing INF-4521 and your tenant id.

Contact / next steps:
- Primary contact for customers: Aisha Patel (customer-success) and oncall SRE lead Marco Ruiz.
- If you see residual issues: open a support ticket at support@redwood.ai with subject: "INF-4521 customer follow-up" and include example request-ids and timestamps.

Notes to internal readers (not for public):
- TODO: prepare per-tenant CSV export script and canned message for customers who ask for impact detail.
summary: Public-friendly status update + short postmortem and a small customer checklist to validate integrations after a routing+KV-cache race caused partial degradation. Drafted for customer success review before publishing to status page and support responses.
